11. Information on Occupied Housing Units
This Chapter discusses detailed information on the occupancy, structure, and condition of housing units.
Furthermore, it examines household data related to main source of drinking water, energy sources used
for daily essentials such as cooking and lighting, and sanitation facilities including toilet usage. Additionally,
the  chapter  covers  household  waste  disposal  methods,  as  well  as  the  availability  of  communication
technology equipment and vehicles.
11.1 Concepts and Definitions
Single housing unit
Housing units that have independent walls not connected to any other housing unit or building vertically or
horizontally, are called 'single housing units’.
Attached housing unit.
If two or more housing units are attached to each other, either horizontally or vertically, each of those
units is considered an attached housing unit.
11.2 Introduction
During  the  listing stage of  the  Census of Population  and Housing  – 2024 all buildings were  listed and
classified into four categories as housing  units,  collective living  quarters, residential  institutes, and non-
residential units. Then at the enumeration stage, in addition to collecting the population data, information
regarding occupied housing units was also collected. Also, data regarding housing units has been collected
in every subsequent census after 1971. The information gathered during the current census, along with the
relevant data analysis, is presented at the district level and categorized by sector namely: Urban, Estate-
Urban, Rural, and Estate-Rural.
During the collection of housing data, information specific to housing units (such as occupancy, structure,
ownership, condition of units, construction materials, and number of rooms) was gathered at the housing
unit  level.  Concurrently,  information  regarding  the  living  conditions  within  those  units  (including  water
supply, cooking fuel, lighting, sanitation, and waste disposal) was collected at the household level.
